human brain\">\n  </figure>\n  <p class=\"drop-cap\">“It is so hard,” the man sitting across from me said. “We’ve been married for nearly fifty years, but I never expected anything like this.”</p>\n  <p>“What is going on?” I asked Al, sympathetically.</p>\n  <p>“It’s Lisa,” he said. “You know her memory has been slipping for a little while. Well, we went to the neurologist like you told us to, and they ordered a whole bunch of tests and a brain scan of some sort. Then, they told her she had dementia.”</p>\n  <p>“I thought that was what was going on,” I replied.</p>\n  <p>“I know you told us that,” Al said. “Well, there are times she doesn’t recognize me. She looks at me blankly like she is wondering what crazy stranger has gotten into her house.”</p>\n  <p>“That’s got to be hard,” I said.</p>\n  <p>“The only thing I’ve found that brings her back to herself is to go outside and call her on her cell phone. I tell her to come out to the garage, I’ve got something to show her. Somehow when I do that, it brings her back to the present and lets her know who I am – for a little bit, anyway.”</p>\n  <p>We moved on to talking about other things, but I could tell that Al’s heart was breaking. His wife of 48 years looked the same as ever on the outside and yet, she was a completely different person.</p>\n  <p>I’d like to explore some of the challenges in dealing with dementia.</p>\n  <h2>Dementia in the Bible</h2>\n  <p>Ecclesiastes 12:1-7 gives a somewhat dismal view of the aging process. “Remember now thy Creator in the days of thy youth, while the evil days come not, nor the years draw nigh, when thou shalt say, I have no pleasure in them; While the sun, or the light, or the moon, or the stars, be not darkened, nor the clouds return after the rain: In the day when the keepers of the house shall tremble, and the strong men shall bow themselves, and the grinders cease because they are few, and those that look out of the windows be darkened, And the doors shall be shut in the streets, when the sound of the grinding is low, and he shall rise up at the voice of the bird, and all the daughters of musick shall be brought low; Also when they shall be afraid of that which is high, and fears shall be in the way, and the almond tree shall flourish, and the grasshopper shall be a burden, and desire shall fail: because man goeth to his long home, and the mourners go about the streets: Or ever the silver cord be loosed, or the golden bowl be broken, or the pitcher be broken at the fountain, or the wheel broken at the cistern. Then shall the dust return to the earth as it was: and the spirit shall return unto God who gave it.”</p>\n  <p>In this passage, the poetic description seems to speak of loss of teeth, loss of hearing, unsteady gait, and general frailty. It is hard to say if any of these images speak of memory loss. What is certain is that the passage begins with a command: “Remember!”</p>\n  <p>This is not the only place in Scripture where humans are commanded to remember. Over and over, we are told to remember God. We are to make certain that we instruct our children about Him. “And thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children, and shalt talk of them when thou sittest in thine house, and when thou walkest by the way, and when thou liest down, and when thou risest up” (Deuteronomy 6:7).</p>\n  <p>The time may come when we are not able to remember anymore. The most important thing – even as we think about the subject of dementia is that we remember the One who made us and follow Him with all our hearts.</p>\n  <h2>What Dementia is</h2>\n  <p>Dementia is any illness that causes a loss of memory, reasoning, and social functioning. Most people think mostly of the loss of memory. I suppose this is because early in the illness other people notice things like difficulty finding words and frequent repetition of stories.</p>\n  <p>Social functioning is often maintained until late in the illness. If you ask someone with mild dementia if they know today’s date, they will likely answer, “Oh, you know, I stopped paying attention to things like that when I retired.”</p>\n  <p>The most common cause of dementia is Alzheimer’s dementia – at least 70 percent of people who have progressive memory loss have Alzheimer’s dementia. Alzheimer’s seems to be related to proteins called amyloid, which get deposited in the brain and prevent nerve cells from communicating with each other.</p>\n  <p>Other causes are vascular dementia, where blockages in the blood vessels in the brain cause the death of nerve cells. Lewy Body Dementia is a sort of memory loss that is associated with Parkinson’s Disease. Approximately eighty percent of people with Parkinson’s Disease will eventually develop dementia.</p>\n  <h2>Diagnosing Dementia</h2>\n  <p>If family members suspect someone is developing memory loss, the best thing is to bring them to their primary care provider for an evaluation. Along with doing a physical exam, the doctor will typically do things like have the patient draw a clock and do a mini mental status exam, which asks the patient to answer a lot of simple questions and do some short-term recall of items.</p>\n  <p>Blood tests including a thyroid and Vitamin B12 level would be done. A brain scan or ultrasound of the neck arteries might be done as well.</p>\n  <p>The goal is to identify areas that can be treated and take care of those.</p>\n  <h2>Eliminate Medications</h2>\n  <figure>\n    <img src=\"/images/articles/e848a36d-36eb-4f7d-aea7-e17ab34a8870-2.jpg\" alt=\"Eyeglasses resting on a stack of books\">\n  </figure>\n  <p>Many medications increase the risk of memory issues. As people get older, trying to avoid these medications is helpful to prevent the development of dementia.</p>\n  <p>Anticholinergic medications are probably the biggest culprit that I encounter. The most common of these medications are older antihistamines like diphenhydramine (used as either a sleep aid or allergy pill) and doxylamine (used as a sleep aid). In one study, patients who took an anticholinergic medication for the equivalent of three years had a significantly higher risk of dementia than patients who took these sorts of medications for less than three months.<sup>1</sup> Older depression medications can also fall into this category.</p>\n  <p>Anxiety medications, called benzodiazepines, have also been associated with memory issues. Studies indicate that patients who take these medications have a higher risk of developing dementia than patients who do not take them.<sup>2</sup></p>\n  <p>Seizure medications may make thinking ability worse as well. Having a seizure disorder seems to increase the risk of dementia, but certain older medications like valproate and gabapentin seem to make it harder for older people to think clearly, and shifting to lower-risk seizure medications is in order (if possible) for older people.</p>\n  <p>There are times when someone needs to take medication, but as patients get older, it is important to think about the risks of those medications. There is a list of medications that are wisest to avoid for patients over 65 years of age, called the Beers List. Substituting similar medications with fewer side effects or using lower doses is recommended.<sup>3</sup></p>\n  <h2>Medical Treatments</h2>\n  <p>The first rule when dealing with dementia is to make certain that all of the metabolic things are in as good control as possible. So, if someone has diabetes, it is best to make certain that their sugar is in as good control as possible. If someone has high blood pressure, make certain that it is well-regulated (this is particularly true if someone has vascular dementia).</p>\n  <p>There are several different classes of medications that are approved for treating dementia. One group is the cholinesterase inhibitors. These medications raise the level of a chemical called acetylcholine in the brain and peripheral nervous system. These medications are certainly not miracle drugs and at best they seem to slow the progression of memory loss and do not really restore previous brain function.</p>\n  <p>The other medication is called memantine. It works by targeting the glutamate receptor in the brain. Just as with the cholinesterase inhibitors, the effects are not huge and the end result only slows the memory loss.</p>\n  <p>Both of these medications are generic, and it is reasonable to try them and see how someone responds to them.</p>\n  <p>One last medication to mention is called lecanemab. It is an IV infusion that targets amyloid, a kind of protein that develops in the brain of people with Alzheimer’s dementia. The medication seems to work quite well at clearing amyloid from patient’s brains. This medication is very expensive ($26,500 per year)and it has been linked to an increase in strokes. In the studies, dementia symptoms were only slowed by about 30 percent compared with a placebo.</p>\n  <p>There are no other medications currently approved to treat dementia.</p>\n  <h2>Non-medication Therapies</h2>\n  <p>There are several things that people can do to help slow the progression of dementia. These can be helpful for people who have a strong family history of dementia and want to prevent its onset.</p>\n  <p>Cardiovascular exercise is very important. Doctors mention exercise in relation to nearly every chronic illness because it has been shown to work. In the case of dementia, people who exercise regularly have about 30 percent decreased risk of developing the disease. Regular exercise seems to slow the progression of dementia.<sup>4</sup></p>\n  <p>Doing puzzles that require mental activity, like Sudoku or crossword puzzles seems to help slow the progression of memory loss and may also reduce the chance of developing dementia.</p>\n  <p>Lastly, it is helpful to learn something new. People who learn a new skill or focus on learning a new language help their memories quite a bit. A study compared older people who learned a new skill with people who went to social events.</p>\n  <p>The point seems to be that our brains need to be pushed to create new pathways or they will tend to break down.<sup>5</sup></p>\n  <h2>Caring For Someone with Dementia</h2>\n  <p>Caring for someone with dementia is challenging in a number of ways. It is often difficult to know how much independence to allow the person. There have been many books written on this subject, but there are a few things that are worth mentioning.</p>\n  <p>It is important to avoid dangerous things. The two most dangerous things for someone with faulty memory are driving and cooking. Both of these seem commonplace, and the person may seem to be doing fine, but they can become a problem very quickly.</p>\n  <p>The danger of driving a car or a buggy is twofold. First, some people freeze at certain points, not remembering how to do a particular skill. This can be a problem, not only for them but also for others on the road.</p>\n  <p>Second, older people can start off on short journeys to a local store or restaurant and end up getting lost. I have had patients who ended up driving around for hours trying to find their way home when they got confused driving to town.</p>\n  <p>Cooking, of course, really comes down to a question of remembering to set timers and take things off the stove or out of the oven at the appropriate time.</p>\n  <p>Many times, people who have dementia do not realize how much their abilities have slipped and resist the idea that they need to give up the car keys. Maybe it simply comes down to a loss of independence, but it is hard to face the fact that you are no longer safe behind the wheel.</p>\n  <p>Try to keep things the same within the room and the home. Even small changes in room arrangement can be enough to upset the situation. Taking someone out of their home – for instance, admitting them to the hospital often makes things a lot worse. Suddenly, confusion that only seemed mild before is now extremely high.</p>\n  <p>If there is a fruit of the spirit that is key for dealing with someone with dementia, it is patience. None of us has as much patience as we need, as dementia spreads that patience awfully thin.</p>\n  <p>People with dementia often act like children on a long trip. They ask over and over when they are going home. They wonder where dead relatives are or why the children aren’t home yet. No amount of explanation helps, because only a minute or two after they ask the question, they have forgotten the answer and are asking again.</p>\n  <p>Their skills often wax and wane. One day, they can button their shirt, and the next day, that skill seems to have flown out the window. It is easy to believe that they aren’t “trying hard” and that they could do more if they would only make the effort.</p>\n  <p>Unfortunately, the fact that someone with dementia could do something yesterday doesn’t mean that they can remember how to do it today. Getting upset with them only makes these things worse as it adds anxiety to a person who already lacks the memory of how to do a skill.</p>\n  <p>As much as possible, answer the person gently even if it is the fifty-third time that you have answered the same question. Use distractions as well. If there is an activity that they can still do, such as sewing or jigsaw puzzles (even children’s puzzles with really big pieces), get them to do it. Late in the illness, letting them look at books with pretty pictures or sometimes even giving them a baby doll to hold can help settle them and distract them from their anxieties of the moment.</p>\n  <h2>Get Others to Help</h2>\n  <p>It is easy to become frustrated. Trying to provide all of the care needed by yourself is not a long-term solution. Dementia care is a marathon and not a sprint. Many people live for years after the diagnosis, and even though their physical body remains relatively strong, they require more and more care.</p>\n  <p>One of the blessings of having family connections and church communities is that we have people who are available to provide assistance.</p>\n  <p>Having family members or friends step in to give you some respite is key to not becoming seriously burned out or even angry with someone that you care about. It is best to take some time away periodically before you are mentally depleted. You may think you are doing fairly well, but all of us have a tendency to get weary in well doing if we never get a break.</p>\n  <h2>Conclusion</h2>\n  <p>I wish there were more medical solutions for dementia. Perhaps more will come later. For now, medications are quite limited.</p>\n  <p>The key is to put the fruit of the Spirit into practice. “But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, meekness, temperance: against such there is no law” (Galatians 5:22-23).</p>\n  <p>Even on the most frustrating days, people who are dealing with severe memory loss need love, gentleness, and patience from their family members. It is only through the Holy Spirit’s power that we can provide the care that is needed for someone whose body is strong, but who no longer even recognizes you.</p>\n  <ol>\n 일이 생길 줄은 전혀 몰랐어.”</p>\n  <p>“무슨 일이 일어나고 있나요?” 나는 알에게 공감하며 물었다.</p>\n  <p>“리사야.” 그가 말했다. “기억력이 조금씩 흐려지는 건 네가 알다시피 있었지. 네가 말한 대로 신경과에 데려갔더니 이것저것 검사하고 뇌 스캔 같은 것도 했대. 그리고 나서 그녀에게 치매가 있다고 말하더군.”</p>\n  <p>“그게 무슨 일인가 싶었어요.” 나는 대답했다.</p>\n  <p>“네가 그렇게 말했단 걸 알아.” 알이 말했다. “어떤 때는 그녀가 나를 알아보지 못할 때가 있어. 그녀는 마치 집에 들어와 있는 낯선 사람이 누구냐고 빈 표정으로 바라봐.”</p>\n  <p>“그건 참 힘들겠네요.” 나는 말했다.</p>\n  <p>“그녀를 지금의 상태로 되돌리는 유일한 방법은 밖으로 나가서 휴대전화로 그녀를 부르는 거야. 차고로 나오라고 하고 보여줄 게 있다고 하지. 이상하게도 그렇게 하면 잠깐 동안 현재로 돌아오고 누군지 알아보더군—어쨌든 잠깐 동안은 말이야.”</p>\n  <p>우리는 다른 이야기들로 화제를 옮겼지만, 알의 마음이 무너지고 있다는 것을 알 수 있었다. 48년간의 아내는 겉모습은 여전했지만 완전히 다른 사람이 되어 있었다.</p>\n  <p>치매를 다루는 데 있어 몇 가지 어려움을 살펴보고자 한다.</p>\n  <h2>성경에서 본 치매</h2>\n  <p>Ecclesiastes 12:1-7 gives a somewhat dismal view of the aging process. “Remember now thy Creator in the days of thy youth, while the evil days come not, nor the years draw nigh, when thou shalt say, I have no pleasure in them; While the sun, or the light, or the moon, or the stars, be not darkened, nor the clouds return after the rain: In the day when the keepers of the house shall tremble, and the strong men shall bow themselves, and the grinders cease because they are few, and those that look out of the windows be darkened, And the doors shall be shut in the streets, when the sound of the grinding is low, and he shall rise up at the voice of the bird, and all the daughters of musick shall be brought low; Also when they shall be afraid of that which is high, and fears shall be in the way, and the almond tree shall flourish, and the grasshopper shall be a burden, and desire shall fail: because man goeth to his long home, and the mourners go about the streets: Or ever the silver cord be loosed, or the golden bowl be broken, or the pitcher be broken at the fountain, or the wheel broken at the cistern. Then shall the dust return to the earth as it was: and the spirit shall return unto God who gave it.”</p>\n  <p>이 구절에서의 시적 묘사는 이빨의 상실, 청력 상실, 불안정한 보행, 전반적인 허약함을 말하는 것처럼 보인다. 이러한 이미지들 중 어느 것이 기억력 상실을 가리키는지는 단정하기 어렵다. 확실한 것은 이 구절이 명령으로 시작한다는 점이다: “기억하라!”</p>\n  <p>성경에서 하나님을 기억하라는 명령은 이곳만이 아니다. 우리는 계속해서 하나님을 기억하라는 지시를 받는다. 자녀들에게 그분에 대해 반드시 가르쳐야 한다. “And thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children, and shalt talk of them when thou sittest in thine house, and when thou walkest by the way, and when thou liest down, and when thou risest up” (Deuteronomy 6:7).</p>\n  <p>기억하지 못하는 때가 올 수 있다. 치매라는 주제를 생각할 때에도 가장 중요한 것은 우리를 지으신 분을 기억하고 온 마음을 다해 그분을 따르는 것이다.</p>\n  <h2>치매란 무엇인가</h2>\n  <p>치매는 기억력, 추론 능력, 사회적 기능의 상실을 초래하는 모든 질병을 말한다. 대부분의 사람들은 주로 기억력 상실을 떠올린다. 아마도 병의 초기에는 말 찾기 어려움이나 이야기의 잦은 반복 같은 것들을 다른 사람들이 먼저 알아차리기 때문일 것이다.</p>\n  <p>사회적 기능은 종종 병의 말기까지 유지된다. 가벼운 치매가 있는 사람에게 오늘 날짜를 아느냐고 물으면, 그들은 대개 “아, 저는 은퇴하고 나서 그런 건 신경 쓰지 않게 되었어요.”라고 대답할 것이다.</p>\n  <p>치매의 가장 흔한 원인은 알츠하이머성 치매다—진행성 기억 상실이 있는 사람들 중 적어도 70퍼센트가 알츠하이머성 치매를 앓는다. 알츠하이머는 아마도 아밀로이드라는 단백질과 관련이 있어, 이 단백질이 뇌에 침착되어 신경세포들이 서로 소통하지 못하게 한다.</p>\n  <p>다른 원인으로는 뇌의 혈관 폐색이 신경세포의 사멸을 일으키는 혈관성 치매가 있다. 루이소체 치매는 파킨슨병과 연관된 일종의 기억 상실이다. 파킨슨병 환자의 약 80퍼센트는 결국 치매를 발병하게 된다.</p>\n  <h2>치매 진단</h2>\n  <p>가족들이 누군가가 기억력 저하를 보인다고 의심하면, 최선의 방법은 일차 진료의에게 평가를 받게 하는 것이다. 신체검사와 함께 의사는 환자에게 시계를 그리게 하거나, 간이 정신상태 검사(Mini Mental Status Exam) 같은 것을 시행해 간단한 질문에 답하게 하고 단기 기억을 검사하는 항목을 요구할 것이다.</p>\n  <p>갑상선 기능과 비타민 B12 수치를 포함한 혈액검사가 이루어질 것이다. 뇌 스캔이나 경동맥 초음파 검사가 시행될 수도 있다.</p>\n  <p>목표는 치료 가능한 부분을 찾아 그것을 관리하는 것이다.</p>\n  <h2>약물 제거하기</h2>\n  <figure>\n    <img src=\"/images/articles/e848a36d-36eb-4f7d-aea7-e17ab34a8870-2.jpg\" alt=\"책 더미 위에 놓인 안경\">\n  </figure>\n  <p>많은 약물이 기억 문제의 위험을 증가시킨다. 사람들이 나이가 들수록 이러한 약물을 피하려고 하는 것이 치매 발병을 예방하는 데 도움이 된다.</p>\n  <p>내가 접하는 가장 큰 범인은 아마도 항콜린성 약물이다. 이 계열의 가장 흔한 약물은 디펜히드라민(수면제나 알레르기 약으로 사용)과 독실아민(수면제로 사용) 같은 오래된 항히스타민제다. 한 연구에서는 항콜린성 약물을 3년 상당 기간 복용한 환자는 이러한 약물을 3개월 미만 복용한 환자보다 치매 위험이 유의하게 높았다.<sup>1</sup> 예전의 일부 우울증 치료제들도 이 범주에 속할 수 있다.</p>\n  <p>불안장애 치료제인 벤조디아제핀 계열 약물도 기억 문제와 관련이 있다. 연구들은 이러한 약을 복용하는 환자가 복용하지 않는 환자에 비해 치매 발병 위험이 더 높다고 보고한다.<sup>2</sup></p>\n  <p>발작 약물도 사고력을 악화시킬 수 있다. 발작장애 자체가 치매 위험을 높이는 경향이 있지만, 발프로에이트나 가바펜틴 같은 일부 오래된 약물은 노인의 사고력을 흐리게 하는 경향이 있어 가능하면 위험도가 낮은 발작 약물로 바꾸는 것이 필요하다.</p>\n  <p>어떤 경우에는 약을 복용해야 할 때가 있지만, 환자가 나이가 들수록 약물의 위험성을 생각하는 것이 중요하다. 65세 이상의 환자가 피하는 것이 좋다고 권고되는 약물 목록이 있는데, 이를 비어스 리스트(Beers List)라고 한다. 부작용이 적은 유사 약물로 대체하거나 용량을 낮추는 것이 권장된다.<sup>3</sup></p>\n  <h2>의학적 치료</h2>\n  <p>치매를 다룰 때의 첫 번째 원칙은 모든 대사적 요인들이 가능한 한 잘 조절되도록 하는 것이다. 따라서 누군가 당뇨병이 있다면 혈당을 가능한 한 잘 관리하는 것이 최선이다. 고혈압이 있다면 잘 조절되었는지 확인하라(이는 특히 혈관성 치매 환자에게 중요하다).</p>\n  <p>치매 치료에 승인된 여러 약물 계열이 있다. 한 그룹은 콜린에스터라제 억제제다. 이 약물들은 뇌와 말초 신경계에서 아세틸콜린이라는 화학물질의 수준을 높인다. 이 약들이 기적적인 약물은 아니며, 최선의 경우 기억력 저하의 진행을 늦출 뿐 이전의 뇌 기능을 복원하지는 못하는 것으로 보인다.</p>\n  <p>다른 약물은 메만틴이라고 불린다. 이것은 뇌의 글루탐산 수용체를 표적으로 작용한다. 콜린에스터라제 억제제와 마찬가지로 그 효과는 크지 않으며 최종적으로는 기억력 저하를 늦출 뿐이다.</p>\n  <p>이들 약물은 모두 제네릭으로 되어 있으며, 시도해보고 환자가 어떻게 반응하는지 보는 것이 합리적이다.</p>\n  <p>언급할 마지막 약물은 레카네맙(lecanemab)이다. 이는 알츠하이머성 치매 환자의 뇌에 생기는 일종의 단백질인 아밀로이드를 표적으로 하는 정맥주사(IV) 제제다. 이 약물은 환자의 뇌에서 아밀로이드를 제거하는 데 꽤 효과적인 것으로 보인다. 이 약은 매우 비싸며(연간 $26,500) 뇌졸중 증가와 연관되어 있다. 연구에서 치매 증상은 위약과 비교했을 때 약 30퍼센트 정도만 늦춰졌다.</p>\n  <p>현재 치매를 치료하도록 승인된 다른 약물은 없다.</p>\n  <h2>약물이 아닌 치료법</h2>\n  <p>치매 진행을 늦추는 데 도움이 될 수 있는 여러 가지 방법이 있다. 강한 가족력 때문에 치매를 예방하고자 하는 사람들에게도 도움이 될 수 있다.</p>\n  <p>심혈관계 운동은 매우 중요하다. 의사들은 거의 모든 만성 질환과 관련하여 운동을 권하는데, 그 효과가 입증되었기 때문이다. 치매의 경우, 규칙적으로 운동하는 사람들은 질병을 발병할 위험이 약 30퍼센트 감소한다. 규칙적인 운동은 치매의 진행을 늦추는 것으로 보인다.<sup>4</sup></p>\n  <p>스도쿠나 십자말풀이처럼 정신적 활동을 요구하는 퍼즐을 하는 것은 기억력 저하의 진행을 늦추는 데 도움이 되며 치매 발병 가능성을 줄일 수도 있다.</p>\n  <p>마지막으로 새로운 것을 배우는 것이 도움이 된다. 새로운 기술을 배우거나 새로운 언어 학습에 집중하는 사람들은 기억력이 상당히 좋아진다. 한 연구는 새로운 기술을 배운 노인들과 사교 모임에 참석한 사람들을 비교했다.</p>\n  <p>요지는 우리 뇌가 새로운 경로를 만들도록 자극받아야 하지 않으면 경로들이 쇠락하는 경향이 있다는 것이다.<sup>5</sup></p>\n  <h2>치매 환자 돌보기</h2>\n  <p>치매 환자를 돌보는 일은 여러 면에서 도전적이다. 그 사람에게 어느 정도의 독립성을 허용할지 판단하기가 종종 어렵다. 이 주제에 관해 쓰인 책들이 많지만, 몇 가지 언급할 가치가 있는 점들이 있다.</p>\n  <p>위험한 것들을 피하는 것이 중요하다. 기억이 흐려진 사람에게 가장 위험한 두 가지는 운전과 요리이다. 둘 다 일상적인 일이기에 그 사람이 잘하는 것처럼 보일 수 있지만, 아주 빠르게 문제가 될 수 있다.</p>\n  <p>자동차나 마차를 운전하는 위험은 두 가지면에서 생긴다. 첫째, 어떤 사람들은 특정 상황에서 얼어붙어 어떤 기술을 어떻게 해야 할지 기억하지 못한다. 이는 그들 자신뿐만 아니라 도로 위의 다른 사람들에게도 문제가 될 수 있다.</p>\n  <p>둘째, 노인들은 근처 상점이나 식당에 잠깐 운전해서 가려다가 길을 잃기 시작할 수 있다. 나는 헷갈려서 집으로 돌아가는 길을 찾으려 몇 시간씩 운전한 환자들을 본 적이 있다.</p>\n  <p>요리는 적절한 시간에 타이머를 맞추고 스토브나 오븐에서 음식을 꺼내는 것을 기억해야 한다는 점에서 문제다.</p>\n  <p>많은 경우, 치매가 있는 사람들은 자신의 능력이 얼마나 떨어졌는지 깨닫지 못하고 자동차 열쇠를 포기해야 한다는 생각을 거부한다. 아마도 단순히 독립성의 상실 때문일 것이다. 그러나 더 이상 운전대 뒤에 서 있는 것이 안전하지 않다는 사실을 인정하기는 어렵다.</p>\n  <p>방과 집 안의 환경을 가능한 한 같게 유지하려고 해라. 방의 배치에 작은 변화만 있어도 상황을 악화시킬 수 있다. 예를 들어, 병원에 입원시키기 위해 집에서 떠나게 하는 것은 상황을 훨씬 더 악화시키는 경우가 많다. 갑자기 이전에는 경미해 보였던 혼란이 매우 심해진다.</p>\n  <p>치매 환자를 대할 때 성령의 열매 중 핵심적인 것은 인내다. 우리 중 누구도 필요한 만큼의 인내를 항상 가진 것은 아니며, 치매가 퍼질수록 그 인내는 얼마나 얇아지는지 모른다.</p>\n  <p>치매 환자들은 종종 긴 여행 중인 아이들처럼 행동한다. 그들은 언제 집에 가느냐고 반복해서 묻는다. 돌아가신 친척들이 어디에 있는지, 왜 아이들이 아직 집에 오지 않았는지 궁금해한다. 아무리 설명해도 소용이 없다. 그들이 질문을 한 지 1~2분 후면 이미 대답을 잊어버리고 다시 묻기 때문이다.</p>\n  <p>그들의 기능은 종종 오르내린다. 어떤 날은 셔츠 단추를 채울 수 있는데 다음 날에는 그 기술이 사라진 것처럼 보인다. 우리는 그들이 ‘노력하지 않는다’고, 더 노력하면 더 할 수 있을 것이라고 생각하기 쉽다.</p>\n  <p>불행히도 어제 할 수 있었던 일이 오늘도 기억해서 할 수 있다는 보장은 없다. 그들에게 화를 내는 것은 상황을 악화시킬 뿐이며 이미 어떻게 하는지 기억하지 못하는 사람에게 불안을 더할 뿐이다.</p>\n  <p>가능한 한 부드럽게 답해라, 비록 같은 질문에 쉰세 번째 대답을 하는 중일지라도. 주의를 돌리는 방법도 사용하라. 그들이 돌봄을 혼자 제공하려고 하는 것은 장기적인 해결책이 되지 못한다. 치매 관리는 단거리 경주가 아니라 마라톤이다. 많은 사람들이 진단 후 수년을 살며, 신체는 상대적으로 강하게 남아 있어도 점점 더 많은 돌봄을 필요로 한다.</p>\n  <p>가족 연결과 교회 공동체가 주는 축복 중 하나는 도움을 제공할 수 있는 사람들이 있다는 것이다.</p>\n  <p>가족 구성원이나 친구들이 교대해 가며 휴식을 줄 수 있도록 하는 것은 심하게 탈진하거나 사랑하는 사람에게 화를 내는 것을 피하는 데 핵심이다. 정신적으로 소진되기 전에 정기적으로 시간을 내어 쉬는 것이 가장 좋다. 자신이 꽤 잘해내고 있다고 생각할지 모르지만, 우리는 모두 쉬지 못하면 선한 일에도 지치기 마련이다.</p>\n  <h2>결론</h2>\n “Adrianna, what’s the temperature outside?” asked Asher. He and Adrianna were sitting at the table doing school with their siblings Emily and Kianna.

“Probably about 50.” Adrianna glanced lazily at the thermometer. “Hey, it’s 65 degrees! Mom, may we eat lunch outside?”

Mom looked up from the sink. “If you do a good job with your school until then, you may,” she told them. “And if you get your school done before lunch, you may play outside for a while this afternoon.”

Asher let out a whoop and started writing fast. The girls grinned at each other and picked up their pencils.

Everyone worked diligently until lunchtime. Then Adrianna made sandwiches while Asher put cookies in bags, Emily collected bags of chips, and Kianna ran down to the basement to grab a few apples. They each packed their lunch in a shopping bag and went out to their picnic spot, a big, flat rock in a clearing in the woods.

They ate quickly, then Adrianna suggested, “Let’s go kayak on the pond!”

“I guess we could,” said Asher slowly. “But didn’t Mom say that Emily and Kianna are too small to handle the kayaks?”

“Oh, yes, I guess she did. Well, they can play on the swings or something,” she shrugged

“I think we should play something everyone can help with,” said Asher. He turned to Emily and Kianna. “What do you want to do?”

“Let’s make a playhouse!” suggested Kianna.

“Yes, let’s!” Emily agreed. “You could hunt for us,” she told Asher.

“And Adrianna could be the mom!” said Kianna.

Adrianna stood with a scowl on her face. Playhouse indeed! She was way too old for that! “I’m going kayaking,” she announced. “You can just have your playhouse.” She picked up her shopping bag and put her sandwich and cookie bags into it. She threw her apple core to the dogs and started for the house.

“Adrianna, can you please take ours too?” begged Emily. “You're going to the house anyway.”

“You can take care of your own stuff,” Adrianna called back, crossly. She dropped her shopping bag on the counter, hoping to slip out of the house before Mom saw her.

She heard her mom’s voice. “Wait, Adrianna, what’s wrong? Your face looks like a thunderstorm!”

Adrianna sighed. She hadn’t been fast enough. “I wanted to go kayaking, but Asher doesn’t want to,” she grumbled.

“Well,” said Mom slowly, “I think Asher is remembering that the other girls can't handle kayaks yet. What are they doing?”

“They’re building a playhouse. I'm way too old for that!” Adrianna burst out.

Mom smiled, “What makes you think that?”

“I'm sure none of the girls my age do stuff like that with their little siblings.”

“Are you sure you're not being selfish?” Mom asked. “Sometimes, we need to give up what we want so that others can be happy.”

Adrianna shrugged and went out to the shed to get a kayak. She lifted her blue kayak off the rack and hauled it down to the pond. She snapped the paddle together, hopped into the seat, and pushed the kayak onto the smooth surface of the water. She sighed with pleasure. This was way better than building a playhouse in the woods! She took a few loops around the pond before her paddle began to slow. Somehow it wasn’t as fun this time. She heard Asher and the girls laughing and shouting as they played. Maybe Mom was right, she thought. Maybe I would be happier if I gave up what I want so that we can all play together. Slowly she paddled to the edge of the pond. She stepped out of the kayak, pulled it out of the water, and flipped it over to dry. Resolutely, she walked out of the pasture to find Asher and the girls.

“Hey! Here comes Adrianna!” called Emily happily as Adrianna walked up.

Adrianna grinned, “It looks like you have your house about set up,” she said encouragingly. “What do you need to finish it?”

“We still need a stove, and something for a countertop,” said Kianna.

“I can help you find something,” Adrianna told them. Together they hunted in the woods and the shed for boards and logs to finish the house. When suppertime came and they went in for supper, Adrianna was very happy. Mom was right, she thought. It is more fun to give up my way and do what everyone else wants to.

Τότε η Αντριάνα έφτιαξε σάντουιτς ενώ ο Άσερ έβαζε μπισκότα σε σακουλάκια, η Έμιλι μάζευε σακουλάκια με πατατάκια και η Κιάνα έτρεξε στο υπόγειο να πάρει μερικά μήλα. Η Αντριάνα στάθηκε με μούτρα. Σπιτάκι παιχνιδιού! Πραγματικά; Ήταν πολύ μεγάλη γι’ αυτό! «Πάω να κάνω κανό», ανακοίνωσε. «Μπορείτε να κρατήσετε το σπιτάκι σας.» Άρπαξε τη σακούλα της και έβαλε μέσα το σάντουιτς και τα μπισκότα. Έριξε το φλούδι του μήλου στους σκύλους και ξεκίνησε για το σπίτι.

«Αντριάνα, μπορείς σε παρακαλώ να πάρεις και τα δικά μας;» παρακάλεσε η Έμιλι. «Πάντως πας στο σπίτι.»

«Μπορείτε να φροντίσετε τα δικά σας», φώναξε η Αντριάνα, θυμωμένα. Έριξε τη σακούλα της πάνω στον πάγκο, ελπίζοντας να βγει απ’ το σπίτι πριν τη δει η μαμά.

Άκουσε τη φωνή της μαμάς. «Περίμενε, Αντριάνα, τι συμβαίνει; Το πρόσωπό σου μοιάζει με καταιγίδα!»

Η Αντριάνα αναστέναξε. Δεν είχε προλάβει αρκετά γρήγορα. «Ήθελα να κάνω κανό, αλλά ο Άσερ δεν θέλει», γκρίνιαξε.

«Λοιπόν», είπε η μαμά αργά, «νομίζω ότι ο Άσερ θυμάται πως τα άλλα κορίτσια δεν μπορούν να χειριστούν ακόμα τα κανό. Τι κάνουν;»

«Φτιάχνουν ένα σπιτάκι παιχνιδιού. Είμαι πολύ μεγάλη γι’ αυτό!» ξέσπασε η Αντριάνα.

Η μαμά χαμογέλασε, «Τι σε κάνει να το νομίζεις αυτό;»

«Είμαι σίγουρη ότι κανένα από τα κορίτσια της ηλικίας μου δεν κάνει τέτοια πράγματα με τα μικρά τους αδελφάκια.»

«Είσαι σίγουρη ότι δεν είσαι εγωίστρια;» ρώτησε η μαμά. «Μερικές φορές πρέπει να παραχωρούμε αυτό που θέλουμε για να είναι κι οι άλλοι χαρούμενοι.»

Η Αντριάνα σήκωσε τους ώμους και πήγε στο υπόστεγο να πάρει ένα κανό. Κατέβασε το μπλε κανό από τη σχάρα και το κουβάλησε μέχρι τη λίμνη. Συναρμολόγησε το κουπί, κάθισε στη θέση και ώθησε το κανό στην ήρεμη επιφάνεια του νερού. Αναστέναξε ευχάριστα. Αυτό ήταν πολύ καλύτερο από το να φτιάχνει ένα σπιτάκι στο δάσος! Έκανε μερικούς κύκλους στη λίμνη πριν το κουπί της αρχίσει να επιβραδύνει. Κάπως δεν ήταν τόσο διασκεδαστικό αυτή τη φορά. Άκουγε τον Άσερ και τα κορίτσια να γελούν και να φωνάζουν καθώς έπαιζαν. Ίσως η μαμά να είχε δίκιο, σκέφτηκε. Ίσως θα ήμουν πιο ευτυχισμένη αν παράχω αυτό που θέλω έτσι ώστε να παίξουμε όλοι μαζί. Αργά κουνούσε το κουπί προς την άκρη της λίμνης. Βγήκε από το κανό, το τράβηξε έξω από το νερό και το γύρισε ανάποδα για να στεγνώσει. Με αποφασιστικότητα, βγήκε από το λιβάδι για να βρει τον Άσερ και τα κορίτσια.

«Κοίτα! Έρχεται η Αντριάνα!» φώναξε η Έμιλι χαρούμενα καθώς η Αντριάνα πλησίαζε.

Η Αντριάνα χαμογέλασε, «Φαίνεται ότι σχεδόν έχετε το σπιτάκι έτοιμο», είπε ενθαρρυντικά. «Τι χρειάζεστε για να το τελειώσετε;»

«Μας χρειάζεται ακόμα μια κουζίνα και κάτι για πάγκο», είπε η Κιάνα.

«Μπορώ να σας βοηθήσω να βρείτε κάτι», τους είπε η Αντριάνα. Μαζί έψαξαν στο δάσος και στο υπόστεγο για σανίδες και κορμούς για να τελειώσουν το σπιτάκι. Όταν ήρθε η ώρα του δείπνου και μπήκαν μέσα για φαγητό, η Αντριάνα ήταν πολύ ευτυχισμένη. Η μαμά είχε δίκιο, σκέφτηκε. Είναι πιο διασκεδαστικό να παραχωρώ τον δικό μου τρόπο και να κάνω ό,τι θέλει όλη η ομάδα.
